data.content_ref: inline:The target asserts expert superiority via 'conditional logic' the checklist allegedly cannot capture, but its own countercondition concedes the point is contingent ('The task is purely algorithmic or additive'). For the class of tasks the problem specifies—'objectively verifiable outcomes'—a large and central subset is exactly algorithmic/additive (e.g., compliance scoring, binary defect detection, structured eligibility checks). On those tasks the target's mechanism ('static checklist... non-expert panel will follow the checklist to a wrong conclusion') provides no reason the panel is worse, so the claim 'a single domain expert will remain more reliable' is unsupported for precisely the task regime the problem foregrounds. The argument only covers the residual non-linear subset and implicitly concedes the rest.
